title: Stream-aware continuous scheduler: memory-aware slot packing for mixed-turn dialogs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Tuning the continuous batching scheduler to reduce GPU memory pressure and tail latency for workloads with high variance between prompt and response lengths (mixed-turn dialogs). This ticket implements stream-aware slot packing heuristics and coordinated KV-cache residency policies to keep per-GPU memory utilization within safe headroom while preserving throughput and SLOs.
background: We observe a recurring pattern where sessions with short prompts but long generated responses (and vice versa) cause slot fragmentation and KV-cache spikes on a subset of GPUs. Current length-prioritized binning reduces mean latency but increases 95/99th percentile due to late-arriving long tails and KV cache churn. Previous efforts focused on length-prioritization and slot coalescing but didn't coordinate with KV residency policies or per-stream prefetch budgets.
goals: 1) Reduce p95/p99 token latency for mixed-length dialog workloads by at least 20% without lowering throughput beyond 5%. 2) Keep peak GPU memory usage under configured headroom (default 90% of allocable memory) to avoid OOM evictions. 3) Maintain or improve token-per-second throughput for bulk inference routes.
proposal: Introduce a stream-aware scheduler mode with three coordinated mechanisms: (A) predictive-slot packing: estimate per-request total token horizon (prompt+expected response length) and prefer packing that minimizes future KV retention; (B) soft-KV residency policy: mark streams with high expected continuation probability as KV-resident and apply early-eviction grace for low-probability streams; (C) adaptive-slot throttling: when GPU memory approaches headroom, throttle admitting new long-horizon slots and favor short-turn coalescing. Scheduler will expose tunables (horizon-confidence, kv-residency-threshold, headroom-percent) and simulate choices on a local admission policy before applying.
implementation_notes:
- Add a per-request horizon estimator based on historical length distributions per route and on-request metadata (user signal: 'expect_long_response' flag).
- Extend slot metadata with horizon_estimate and kv_hint fields.
- Modify slot packing algorithm to prefer groupings that reduce cumulative KV lifetime on each GPU (cost function = sum(kv_lifetime_bytes * probability_of_continuation)).
- Implement a KV-residency controller that holds small bloom-of-streams for reservation and exposes eviction candidates to eviction watcher.
- Add a GPU headroom monitor and admission controller that applies adaptive-slot throttling when memory > headroom_percent.
- Telemetry: per-slot kv_lifetime_estimate, eviction_count_by_reason, admission_reject_count, p50/p95/p99 token latency per route, and per-GPU peak mem percent.
- Backwards compatibility: default mode remains current continuous-batcher; stream-aware mode behind runtime flag and feature gate.
- Rollback plan: if p99 latency increases or OOMs observed, disable stream-aware mode and revert config server flags.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature gated prototype in internal canary pool (1-2 GPUs) with synthetic mixed-turn workloads. 2) Controlled canary: enable for 5% of production traffic on non-critical routes for 48 hours. 3) Broader rollout to 25% with monitoring for 7 days. 4) Full rollout if metrics pass. 5) Post-rollout: iterate tunables and add auto-tune job.
Monitoring gates: no increase in OOMs, p99 token latency improvement >=15% on canary routes, throughput loss <5%.
metrics:
- p50/p95/p99 token latency per route (pre/post).
- Peak GPU memory percent (per-GPU).
- KV-residency count and eviction rate.
- Admission rejects and throttling duration.
- Tokens/sec per GPU and overall throughput.
- Error rate and OOM events.
risks:
- Incorrect horizon estimates may misclassify long conversations, increasing tail latency.
- Aggressive KV residency could increase memory pressure and cause OOMs if headroom misconfigured.
- Complexity in packing cost function may add CPU overhead to scheduler path, potentially increasing admission latency.
- Edge cases: multimodal requests or streaming tool-calls altering expected response sizes.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Deployed in canary pool and synthetic workload shows >=20% p99 improvement.
2) Production canary (5%) shows no OOMs and p99 improvement >=15% on targeted routes.
3) Throughput degradation <=5% measured at tokens/sec.
4) Observability shows correct telemetry and alerting for headroom breaches and eviction spikes.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for horizon estimator and packing cost function.
- Integration test: simulate mixed-turn traces against scheduler in local harness measuring mem and latency.
- Load test: run synthetic workloads with skewed turn distributions on CI cluster.
- Chaos test: force KV eviction and ensure graceful degradation path.
- Canary monitoring playbook defined with runbook links.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Liam Chen: Spike completed. Horizon estimator prototype using exponential moving average + route priors looks promising. Initial mem model underestimates KV bytes for quantized shards; need conservative multiplier.
2026-02-22 - Priya Kapoor (PM): Make sure we expose per-route override and an opt-out flag for enterprise customers that require strict determinism.

2026-02-28 - Engineering review: Discussed cost function. Decided to use probability-weighted KV-lifetime to prefer packing shorter-horizon streams. Action: add a lightweight continuation predictor using last-K turns feature vector.
2026-03-03 - Design feedback (Sofia R.): UX for operator console should surface headroom percent and top eviction reasons per GPU. Add a visualization for slot lifetime heatmap.

2026-03-07 - Liam Chen: Implemented admission controller and headroom monitor. Running synthetic mixed-turn load on canary pool. Observed p95 down 18%, p99 down 12% — close to target. Submitted PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2873
2026-03-10 - QA: Early canary running at 5% production traffic on chat-route. No OOMs observed so far; minor increase in scheduler CPU (~6%). Monitoring retention for 48h.
Notes: If scheduler CPU becomes a bottleneck, we will offload horizon estimation to a sampling worker and cache results for short durations.
Follow-ups: auto-tuning job to periodically adjust headroom-percent and kv-residency-threshold by route; tie to rollout canary metrics.
